recommendation_summary: The reply recommends one dead-man's-switch heartbeat (for example healthchecks.io) that `nightly-sync` pings when it succeeds, so the user gets an email or text if no ping arrives by 03:10.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You asked to know when `nightly-sync` dies, without reading logs yourself. Nobody has asked for centralized logging as an end in itself, that's a proposed means.
labels.Deleted: A Synology Docker log-aggregation stack (Loki/Grafana, ELK, etc.). It solves "where do logs live," not "who notices a silent failure," and still requires you to go look at a dashboard, which you said you won't do.
labels.Bottleneck: Nothing alerts when the job fails before it reaches the email step. That's the entire four-day gap. Everything else about the job already works.
labels.Checked myself: From what you told me, cron starts the job at 03:00 on `edna`, it emails on completion, last week it died at startup four nights running before the email step, and nothing else watches it today.

note: I counted this as one alert because the self-hosted Synology version is offered only instead of healthchecks.io, not in addition, and the reply explicitly says 'no new host, no Docker stack'.
